verdicts.misleading_risk: Partly misleading as written. The auditor says all three READMEs say Intel is unsupported, but VLab4Mic's README contradicts itself. Line 39 (live and local clone) says '.pkg (ARM64 or Intel) ... Pick ARM64 for Apple silicon, Intel otherwise', and line 47 says 'Intel Macs are not supported'. So for VLab4Mic the site cannot tell which is true, and any author field the site adds only becomes true once the author decides. GuessTheCondition README:49 and Playground README:32 are verified and unambiguous. Neither app's manifest mentions Intel. The 'absent: say the author does not list supported systems' line would add a negative notice to every one of the six apps (CellTracksColab, NucleiSky and Demo ship Intel without complaint), which is noise and states a non-fact about the author.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Keep it small and author-driven. (1) Add an optional `distribution.platforms` list to labconstrictor-app.schema.json (enum windows-x86_64, macos-arm64, macos-x86_64, linux-x86_64). (2) In cards.downloads(), when the field is present, keep only the listed primary assets with an explicit `in` test. If a listed platform has no asset in the release, raise AppProblem naming the app, as catalogue.read_release does. When the field is absent, offer every asset exactly as today, with no extra wording. That is documented behaviour, not a silent fallback, so state it in the schema description and in content/submit.md. (3) Apply the same filter in downloads_table(), so the table does not offer a file the tiles hide. lc.js needs no change because it reads data-arch from the tiles. (4) Add tests for present, absent and listed-but-missing. (5) The Mac tile shows 'Intel Macs: not supported by this app' only when macos-arm64 is listed and macos-x86_64 is not. (6) Then ask the GuessTheCondition and Playground authors to add the list, and ask VLab4Mic to resolve README lines 39 vs 47 first. Do not add the site's own claim for any app. Do not edit data/site.yaml:20, since it describes what the template builds, which is true. The template and initialiser change (skip the Intel build) is a separate upstream task, not part of this site change.
verdicts.evidence: cards.py:107-117 lists every `primary` asset. schema line 28 has only `installer: const true`. build/snapshot.json shows MacOSX-x86_64.pkg and .sh in the releases of guessthecondition, labconstrictor-playground and labconstrictor-vlab4mic. GuessTheCondition/README.md:49 and the live Playground README:32 say Intel is not supported. The live VLab4Mic README (CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor-VLab4Mic) line 39 says 'ARM64 or Intel' and line 47 says 'Intel Macs are not supported'. The release_constructor.yml of GuessTheCondition and VLab4Mic still builds macos-15-intel. The site has no way to hide an asset. pages_apps.py is 208 lines and cards.py 135, so there is room under the 300-line limit.

verdicts.misleading_risk: The base proposal is fine, but two parts invent or overstate. `verified_systems` is a new registry field that nobody can fill from a source, so a 'tested OS' claim would be unverified: drop it. 'Windows 64-bit (Intel/AMD)' and 'x86_64 only' are verifiable from the asset names and from lc.js:46, so they are safe. Do not restate the Gatekeeper steps on the app page, because the install guide already has them (install/index.md:139, 146, 155-156, 161) and a second copy would drift.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Do only the cheap, verifiable parts. (1) Put one line directly under the 'Get it' h2, in a small function: 'v0.1.1 · 7 July 2026 · files come from github.com/<repo>/releases', built from release_line(app) and app['repo'], shown only when a release exists. (2) Change the Windows hint (pages_apps.py:67) to something like 'The installer is not code-signed, so Windows may warn you. Run files only from this app's GitHub release. See the install guide.' It must link to guides/install/, which already says this. (3) Add 'Needs a terminal.' to the Linux hint and 'Windows and Linux builds are 64-bit Intel/AMD (x86_64)' to the Windows and Linux tiles. (4) Add one macOS sentence pointing to the guide: 'If macOS refuses to open it, see the install guide.' (5) megabytes(): text.py:55-57 divides by 2**20 but prints 'MB'. Pick one convention and make the label match it, either dividing by 10**6 or printing MiB, and update the docstring and tests. This is a real inaccuracy, but it is low priority. Skip `verified_systems`. Rephrase the Details 'Status' row only if a maintainer ever supplies the data.
verdicts.evidence: pages_apps.py:64-69 (os_tile hints: Windows 'If Windows warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway.', Linux 'Run it with: bash <file name>', macOS chip hint only). The Get it block has no version or date. pages_apps.py:128 holds the date in 'All downloads' and release_line() in Details. text.py:55-57 megabytes() uses 2**20. docs/guides/install/index.md:139 ('not code-signed yet... Download only from the app's own GitHub release'), :155 ('Open Anyway'), :156 ('Applications folder'), :161 (terminal). So the information exists but is one click away, not on the tile.

verdicts.misleading_risk: A PyPI fetch adds a new network edge, a SNAPSHOT_FORMAT bump and a second source for pip metadata, for one app. An author-written `data_note` adds a field nobody has asked for. A site-wide Colab sentence is safe only if it is limited to facts true of every Colab notebook. 'Files you upload or connect (for example Google Drive) leave your computer' is true for notebooks that use them, but not every notebook mounts Drive, so word it generically.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Two small edits in get_section/notebooks_list. (1) Under the 'Notebooks to open in your browser' heading add one generic line: 'These run on Google's servers in Google Colab: you need an internet connection and a Google account, and any data you load into the notebook is handled by Google. The desktop app runs on your computer.' (2) Label the pip block: a heading 'Python package (advanced)', the exact command as today, and a line 'The package named by the author on PyPI; it may not match the desktop app's version.' with a link to https://pypi.org/project/<name>/ so the visitor can see the version and Python requirement. Do not add the PyPI JSON fetch or `data_note`. Add a test that a manifest with `colab` renders the sentence, and that `pip` renders the label. Update the DESIGN.md route-block rule in the same change. If an author later wants app-specific facts such as 'mounts your Drive', add `data_note` then.
verdicts.evidence: pages_apps.py:103-104 prints the bare `pip install nucleisky` under the Colab list with no label. notebooks_list() is only a heading plus rows. The only Colab sentence in content/guides/using-apps.md is line 15, which says nothing about accounts or data. GuessTheCondition README:53 says the notebook 'mounts your Google Drive' and CellTracksColab README:102 says data is 'Uploaded to your Google Drive' versus 'Stays on your computer'. PyPI nucleisky (fetched live) shows version 0.0.1, requires_python >=3.12 and the summary 'Constellation-based point-set registration utilities for microscopy in 2D and 3D', while the page shows the 0.1.1 release. NucleiSky README:50 and :53 tell users to `pip install nucleisky` and `nucleisky[all]`. So the mismatch is real, but a link to PyPI plus a label is enough.

verdicts.misleading_risk: Low if the chip reads the plugin's own status. It would be misleading if it implied that the app's tools are tested in that host. The status describes the plugin, not each app. The 'tested on Linux only' line comes from guide prose, and extracting it from the guide's first paragraph is fragile and is a retyped second description, so skip it. `tested_with` needs edits in three other repos for little gain.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Replace the hard-coded 'Soon in X' (cards.py:64-71, tooltip and screen-reader text included) with text derived from the plugin's project status: hosts.yaml `plugin` -> projects.load_project(repo)['status']. Use a small explicit mapping with an error on an unknown value, for example Experimental -> 'Experimental in napari', Available -> 'Works in napari', Install from GitHub -> 'In napari (install from GitHub)', Deprecated -> 'napari plugin deprecated'. Keep the badge linked to the guide, which carries the caveats. Change DESIGN.md:32 and :49 and AGENTS.md:29 first, in the same PR, because they name 'Soon in napari' as the pattern. Reword data/site.yaml:8 ('Soon, apps can also work inside...') to match. Optionally add maturity to the Details 'Works in' row, so the filter and the pills agree with the cards. Do not add per-app host-testing claims or `tested_with`.
verdicts.evidence: cards.py:64-71 hard-codes 'Soon in {HOSTS[key]}' in the tooltip, the sr text and the badge. DESIGN.md:32 and :49 and AGENTS.md:29 name the pattern. data/site.yaml:8 says 'Soon'. docs/labconstrictor-project.yaml of napari-labconstrictor, LabConstrictor-Fiji and LabConstrictor-QuPath each say `status: Experimental` (I read all three). The built Ecosystem page says 'These plugins are untested and under heavy construction.' The project schema already restricts status to Experimental, Available, Install from GitHub or Deprecated. hosts.yaml gives each host a `plugin` repo. The built /apps/guessthecondition/ page shows 'Soon in napari'. I did not re-check the QuPath guide's 'JDK 25' or the 'Tested on Linux' statement.
